rules.purpose: Single list of every image in Moonbeam Colony. The art tools (tools/art/render.py, gallery.py, previews.py) and later the game's asset manifest read this file. Every entry is drawn as SVG in this repo: art/svg/<family>/ (house style art/STYLE.md) -> tools/art/render.py -> appPath. Sizes, anchors and names came from the superseded ChatGPT pack (docs/art/chatgpt-asset-prompts.md) and plan D10; values not stated there are marked 'derived' in notes.
sources: docs/plan/E-architecture.md (E.2.3 /assets/*, E.8.2 per-planet atlas from the asset manifest)
docs/art/chatgpt-asset-prompts.md (superseded; origin of the sizes, anchors and the 'conversation' and 'card' values)
rules.entries: One entry per shipped still image, and one entry per animation. Animations are NOT expanded: they give 'frames' (count) and 'framePattern', where {nn} is the two-digit frame number 01..frames (D10.1 '<assetId>-<anim>-<nn>.png'). For an animation, 'file' is frame 01's name. Reference images that are never shipped (style anchor, character sheets, alien line-up, height guide, Glorp base) are included so progress can be tracked; they have appPath and atlas null.
rules.id: Unique per entry, ^[a-z0-9-]{1,40}$ (spine S9.5): the file name without extension and without the -<nn> frame suffix. For animations this is '<D10 assetId>-<anim>' (for example nova-l1-attack for D10 asset nova-l1). Exceptions, where the PNG already uses the plain name and the extension is added to the id: logo-svg (logo.svg), logo-on-dark-svg (logo-on-dark.svg), luna-backdrop-png (luna-backdrop.png, the fallback of luna-backdrop.webp).
rules.conversation: Historical: the ChatGPT conversation from the superseded pack 1.3 ('0', '1'..'6', '7a'..'7c', '8a'..'8c', '9a', '9b', '10'..'14', '15-17'), or null. Kept only to cross-reference the pack's cards; no tool uses it.
rules.source: 'drawn-svg' = drawn as vector SVG in this repo (art/svg/<family>/<file stem>.svg, one SVG per frame) and rendered by tools/art/render.py. Every entry uses it. 'css' = drawn by CSS at runtime (no entry uses it; reserved). Earlier values 'chatgpt' and 'svg' were retired when all art was drawn in-repo.
rules.canvas: Historical: the ChatGPT canvas from the superseded pack 1.4, or null. Not used; render.py renders at authorSize.
rules.sizes: displaySize = [w,h] in game/CSS px on the 1920x1056 logical canvas. authorSize = the 2x master the game ships (D10.1, pack 1.4), so authorSize = 2 x displaySize unless the card says otherwise (Juno blast 269 -> 538; backdrop 3840x2112). Where a card gives a range (64-128, 128-256) the top of the range is used so the game only ever shrinks. For SVG, authorSize is only the raster size for placeholders and any PNG fallback.
rules.anchor: [x,y] normalised 0..1 from the top-left of the authorSize image. [0.5,1] bottom-centre for astronauts, aliens, bosses and things standing on the ground (feet on the route or pad; flyers keep it with the body drawn high, for shadow placement); [0.5,0.5] centre for effects, icons, pads, route tiles and flat ground items (D10.1); [0,0.5] left-middle for beams and tracers stretched from the gadget to the target at runtime; the drawn ground centre (about [0.5,0.62]) for flat items drawn 'centred low' (portal-idle, fx-place). Exceptions are marked 'derived' in notes.

transparency.alpha: real transparency expected; made by the owner (SVG or editor), so no keying
transparency.key-green: ask ChatGPT for transparency; if the raw has no real alpha it was made on flat #00FF00, which the tool keys out (pack 1.5)
transparency.key-magenta: as key-green but the fallback is flat #FF00FF, for green or lime subjects (pack 1.5)
transparency.black-screen: glow or translucent effect generated on flat #000000; the tool converts black to alpha, or the game draws it with additive/screen blending (pack 1.5, 4.5)
transparency.none: opaque image (backdrops, screen backgrounds, reference sheets)
transparency.alpha-required: the subject contains both lime/green and magenta, so neither key is safe: the raw must have real alpha; the tool fails (reports the file) instead of keying, and the owner regenerates or cuts it out by hand
transparency._note: Historical: describes how ChatGPT raws would have been keyed. The drawn SVGs render with real alpha (render.py uses a transparent background), so no keying happens; opaque images ('none') draw their own background.

rules.atlas: 'atlas-common' (astronauts, aliens, bosses, effects, powers) and 'atlas-luna-1' (Moonbeam map, colony, pads, decorations) are packed sprite atlases (D10.1). 'ui' and 'activity' are loose files served from those folders (DOM images). null = not packed (backdrop, full-screen overlays) or not shipped. The tool may split an atlas into pages if it exceeds the texture size limit (the 768 px boss frames are large).
rules.rawPath: For reference images that are never shipped (appPath null), the PNG that tools/art/render.py writes (art/source/...). For every other entry it is the superseded ChatGPT raw location and is not used; the source is art/svg/<family>/<file stem>.svg.
rules.appPath: web/player/public/assets/<group>/<file or framePattern> with group luna-1 | common | ui | activity (pack 1.6, a proposal that section E owns). tools/art/render.py writes these: raster files rendered at authorSize, and .svg entries copied as-is. The game's asset-manifest.json is built later (build Phase 64).

required.M1: replace these placeholders first: art the first playable slice shows on screen (J M1-21, B3.2: one route, a few pads, Nova L1, Moon Blob, the colony and its damage states, defeat and leak effects, profile avatars, the sync chip (SYNCED, PENDING, RETRYING, AUTH_REQUIRED), a few HUD and Play icons, and the attempt and reward feedback of the one M1 activity ph-0102, which has no picture). B3.2 says M1 art is labelled placeholders, so M1 here means 'replace placeholders first', not 'blocks M1'
required.core: needed for the full planned game
required.optional: the pack marks it optional or reuses other art first

rules.placeholders: Until an entry's rendered file exists at appPath, the game draws a labelled placeholder (coloured shape with the id) at authorSize and anchor, so building never waits for art (D10, prompt.md:1066). All 352 entries are drawn, so this applies only to entries added later.
rules.progress: An entry is drawn when its SVG source exists in art/svg/<family>/ for every frame 01..frames (python3 tools/art/render.py --check lists gaps), and rendered when its file exists at appPath (or rawPath for reference images).
notEnumerated: activity.pic.age67-nouns: about 8 more pic-<word>.png, chosen when the age 6-7 banks are authored (128, author 256, key-green, activity)
activity.demo.cards: demo-<conceptId>-<nn>.png, about 20, 256 (author 512), defined as concepts are authored
excluded: class.all.selected: runtime tint and outline, no file
hit flash, slowed tint and selection glow: runtime tints (D10.1)
sounds and phonics clips: not images
rules.standPoint: optional, pads only: [x,y] normalised point on the pad's top surface where a placed astronaut's anchor goes. Needed because a three-quarter pad shows its sides, so the standing surface is above the image centre
rules.animGroup: optional: stills that the game plays as a loop although they have their own file names (deco-lamp-on then deco-lamp-off, the card's '2-frame blink'). Entries sharing an animGroup form one animation, ordered by animFrame (1..n)
rules.framePattern: present only on animations (frames > 1); stills leave it out, so validators treat it as optional
